recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-14806 unless PA opens a new tracker to revisit the broader Appointment.start/end versus Encounter.actualPeriod wording.
issue_request: FHIR-14806 was a Published PA change request, resolved Not Persuasive with Modification, asking for actual start/end support when Appointment.minutesDuration is less than the difference between Appointment.start and Appointment.end. The accepted resolution said actual occurrence timing belongs on the resulting Encounter, planned appointment timing remains on Appointment, and Appointment.minutesDuration should include examples where duration legitimately differs from the start/end interval without adding an invariant.
initial_application: Historical commit 1ced9ed8a81e6aec9e55edf8075dcb5b1f22330f explicitly applied GF#14806 to source/appointment/appointment-spreadsheet.xml by changing the Appointment.minutesDuration short and definition text. Later source-format refactors, including the R4B conversion to structuredefinition-Appointment.xml and generated mapping-exception files, preserved that wording.
additional_context: Appointment and Encounter are active resources in source/fhir.ini. Current Appointment narrative says the resource represents an intention and that fulfillment details are handled by Encounter, and current Encounter.actualPeriod defines the actual start and end time of the encounter. Later Published issue FHIR-36814 moved Appointment.requestedPeriod near start/end and added start/end comments, but did not remove or supersede the FHIR-14806 minutesDuration examples.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current Appointment.minutesDuration definition already contains the examples requested by FHIR-14806, the Appointment narrative points fulfillment details to Encounter, and Encounter.actualPeriod supplies the actual timing field identified by the resolution.

related_jiras.note: Later Published Appointment timing issue that moved requestedPeriod and added Appointment.start/end comments; it affects surrounding wording but does not supersede the FHIR-14806 duration guidance.
